sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Pierrebraunia bahiensis is a succulent cactus endemic to Bahia in north-eastern Brazil, where it grows on rocky outcrops in seasonally dry habitats. Young globose stems become cylindrical; they often reach about 30 cm, with older plants growing larger.

sections.title: Stems, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The stems, about 8 cm across, usually have 9–14 rounded ribs, woolly areoles when young and spines. The tubular pink flowers are about 3.2–3.9 cm long and open at night; the fruit is a pink berry.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable human food use was found for this species.
